#!/bin/bash
# =============================================================================
# devhost — run agent dev work on the BUILD HOST (node-2), not on the primary.
#
# Edit files on the primary as usual (your own git worktree — never /opt/nxeon),
# then run every heavy command through this helper. It mirrors your worktree's
# source to node-2 (/tank/nxeon-build/wt/<name>, own node_modules there), runs the
# command inside the capped nxeon-build-agents.slice with a THROWAWAY database
# (Postgres on node-2 127.0.0.1:5433), and streams the output back.
#
#   scripts/devhost run [--lock] [--max SEC] -- CMD...   push + run CMD in the node-2 copy
#   scripts/devhost tsc                                  = run -- npx tsc --noEmit
#   scripts/devhost test [FILES...]                      = run --lock -- npx tsx --test ...
#   scripts/devhost build                                = run --lock -- npx next build
#   scripts/devhost dev [--port P]                       start `next dev` on node-2 (background unit)
#   scripts/devhost bg NAME [--port P] -- CMD...         any background process (worker, preview server)
#   scripts/devhost stop [NAME|all]                      stop this worktree's background units
#   scripts/devhost logs [NAME] [-n N] [-f]              journal of a background unit (default: dev)
#   scripts/devhost tunnel PORT [LOCAL_PORT]             ssh -L so the primary can curl/Playwright it
#   scripts/devhost pull REMOTE_PATH [LOCAL_DEST]        copy results (screenshots, reports) back
#   scripts/devhost push                                 just sync files (run does this itself)
#   scripts/devhost install                              force npm install + prisma generate there
#   scripts/devhost db push|reset|info                   throwaway DB: schema push / recreate / name
#   scripts/devhost env set KEY=VALUE | unset KEY | list extra env for this worktree (never prod secrets)
#   scripts/devhost rm                                   stop units, drop the throwaway DB, delete the node-2 copy
#   scripts/devhost ls | status | sync                   workspaces / node-2 load / push refs to node-2's mirror
#
# Rules: /root/agent-notes/BUILD-HOST.md. The node-2 copy is a build/run sandbox,
# not a place to edit or commit — your primary-side worktree stays the source of truth.
# =============================================================================
set -euo pipefail
HERE="$(dirname "$(readlink -f "$0")")"
# shellcheck source=lib/buildhost-env.sh
source "$HERE/lib/buildhost-env.sh"
REPO="${DEVHOST_REPO:-/opt/nxeon}"

die() { echo "devhost: $*" >&2; exit 1; }
say() { echo "devhost: $*" >&2; }
q() { printf '%q ' "$@"; }

# ---- workspace identity -----------------------------------------------------
worktree_root() {
  local top; top=$(git rev-parse --show-toplevel 2>/dev/null) || die "run this inside your own git worktree of the Nxeon repo"
  top=$(readlink -f "$top")
  case "$top" in
    /opt/nxeon|/opt/nxeon-staging|/tank/nxeon-deploy/*) die "$top is a live/deploy tree. Create your own worktree first:  git -C /opt/nxeon worktree add /tank/dev-worktrees/<name> -b <branch> main" ;;
  esac
  [ -L "$top/.next" ] && die "$top/.next is a symlink (a live tree) — refusing"
  [ -L "$top/node_modules" ] && say "warning: $top/node_modules is a symlink — never 'git add -A' here (see BUILD-HOST.md). devhost does not need local node_modules at all."
  echo "$top"
}
ws_name() {
  local top="$1" n
  n=$(basename "$top" | tr 'A-Z' 'a-z' | tr -c 'a-z0-9-\n' '-' | sed -E 's/-+/-/g; s/^-//; s/-$//' | cut -c1-40)
  [ -n "$n" ] || n=wt
  echo "${DEVHOST_NAME:-$n}"
}
init_ws() {
  TOP=$(worktree_root); NAME=$(ws_name "$TOP")
  case "$NAME" in *[!a-z0-9-]*|"") die "bad workspace name '$NAME' (DEVHOST_NAME=...)";; esac
# BUILD HOST — all builds and heavy dev work run on node-2, not the primary

**Since 2026-10-07 (owner decision).** The primary (ns5002569, 51.79.162.96) only serves the live site:
prod web/worker, Postgres, customer VMs. Parallel agent builds there pushed load to 16+, filled swap
and hard-crashed it on 2026-10-06. Everything heavy now runs on **node-2 = nxeon-fsn1
(178.63.94.114)**, inside a capped systemd slice.

Full technical write-up: `docs/DOCUMENTATION.md` → "Build host (node-2)".

## What runs where

| Work | Where | How |
|---|---|---|
| Production / staging release builds (`npm install`, `prisma generate`, `next build`) | node-2, `nxeon-build-prod.slice` | automatically by `scripts/promote-production.sh` / `scripts/deploy-staging.sh` |
| Schema push, pre-cutover smoke (:3095), cutover, restarts, rollback | primary | same scripts, unchanged |
| Agent `tsc`, tests, `next build`, `next dev`, Playwright, throwaway DBs | node-2, `nxeon-build-agents.slice` | `scripts/devhost` (below) |
| Editing files, git commits | primary, in **your own worktree** | as before |

## Caps on node-2 (it also runs ~13 customer VMs — never touch them)

- `nxeon.slice` CPUWeight 20 / IOWeight 10 (VMs in `qemu.slice` win any contention ~5:1)
- `nxeon-build.slice`: **CPUQuota 900 % (9 of 12 threads, raised 2026-10-08), MemoryMax 10 G, MemoryHigh 9.5 G, no swap**
  - `nxeon-build-prod.slice`: release builds — CPUWeight 1000, MemoryLow 6 G, oom_score_adj 500
  - `nxeon-build-agents.slice`: agent work — **MemoryMax 7 G**, oom_score_adj 1000 (dies first)
- every process: nice 10, ionice best-effort 7. Build files live on `tank` (separate SATA SSD);
  VMs are on `rpool` (NVMe), so build IO never hits their disks.
- **Build lock** on node-2: `/run/lock/nxeon-build.lock` — one heavy job at a time
  (release builds, `devhost build|test`, `devhost run --lock`). Locked agent jobs are capped at
  25 min by default so a promote (waits max 30 min) is never starved.

## How agents work from now on

1. Make your own worktree on the primary (never work in `/opt/nxeon` or `/opt/nxeon-staging`):
   `git -C /opt/nxeon worktree add /tank/dev-worktrees/<name> -b <branch> main`
   You do NOT need `node_modules` in it (and never symlink one in).
2. Edit with your normal tools. Then, from inside the worktree, run heavy things on node-2:
   ```
   /opt/nxeon/scripts/devhost tsc                    # npx tsc --noEmit
   /opt/nxeon/scripts/devhost test [test/x.test.ts]  # tsx --test (takes the build lock)
   /opt/nxeon/scripts/devhost build                  # next build (takes the build lock)
   /opt/nxeon/scripts/devhost run -- <cmd...>        # anything else; add --lock if heavy
   /opt/nxeon/scripts/devhost db push                # schema into YOUR throwaway DB
   /opt/nxeon/scripts/devhost dev                    # next dev on node-2 127.0.0.1:<port>
   /opt/nxeon/scripts/devhost tunnel <port>          # reach it from the primary (curl/Playwright)
   /opt/nxeon/scripts/devhost run -- npx playwright test ...   # or run Playwright ON node-2
   /opt/nxeon/scripts/devhost pull <path> [dest]     # copy screenshots/reports back
   /opt/nxeon/scripts/devhost stop [name|all]        # ALWAYS stop dev servers when done
   /opt/nxeon/scripts/devhost rm                     # when finished: units, DB and node-2 copy gone
   /opt/nxeon/scripts/devhost status                 # node-2 load, slice memory, lock, running units
   ```

202:export const pcmSha256 = (x: Mono) => createHash("sha256").update(toS16(x)).digest("hex");
/**
 * The Cyrus mark — a stylised "Y" built on a strict grid.
 *
 * Construction (design space 1000 × 600, centre 500,300):
 *  - The SWEEP is a band at -40.4° (run 1.176 : rise 1) whose two edges pass 120 units apart
 *    horizontally (≈78 thick). Both ends taper to hairline points that settle onto horizontals,
 *    and the whole shape is point-symmetric about the centre.
 *  - The ARM is the mirror-angle band (≈71 thick — a step lighter than the sweep), with the same
 *    hairline taper at the top-left and a true semicircular cap that stops exactly 20 units short
 *    of the sweep, so the Y reads as two precise strokes rather than a blob.
 *
 * Rendering is layered for a glass-tube look: a vivid base gradient, a cylindrical shade across
 * each band (lit from the top edge), a specular streak, and a crisp edge. The same markup feeds
 * the React component and the WebGL core's texture, so the logo is identical everywhere.
 */

export const MARK_VIEWBOX = "20 40 940 520";
export const MARK_ASPECT = 940 / 520;

export const MARK_SWEEP =
  "M940 60 C880 62 766 124 736 150 L337 490 C307 516 240 540 180 540 L60 540 C120 538 234 476 264 450 L663 110 C693 84 760 60 820 60 Z";
export const MARK_ARM = "M40 60 L140 60 C190 60 233 80 262 105 L418 238 A35.6 35.6 0 0 1 372 292 L205 150 C174.5 124 100 62 40 60 Z";

content.thinking:
I'm thinking through the visual design for the mod assets—figuring out how to represent a banshee skin using zombie-base mob UV mapping and pairing it with a handgun texture, since the tool is more item-focused than mob-skin-focused.

I'll scope it down: a "Banshee Veil" drop item at 16x16 as the authored texture asset, a Glock 9mm handgun item with fire/reload sound events, and the banshee mob listed with its skin/UV question flagged as open rather than implemented, plus a style DNA entry covering outline color and shading ramps for the mod.

Now I'm sketching the design tokens for the mockups themselves: a deep near-black background, glassy violet-tinted surfaces, violet as the single accent with cyan reserved for live/playhead states and pink used sparingly, paired with Inter/Space Grotesk/JetBrains Mono typography and consistent panel/chip radii — aiming for a calm studio backdrop with just a hint of aurora and a dimmed network map.

For the layout itself, I'm deciding to keep the Cyrus topbar with its breadcrumb trail and right-side chips, plus a slim 56px dark portal rail on the left rather than stacking both the portal's and Cyrus's top bars, since that would eat too much vertical space.

Now I'm fleshing out the Texture Studio at 1440x900: a 64px Cyrus topbar, a 52px glass tool rail on the left with pencil/eraser/fill/picker/select/line/rect/mirror tools plus zoom controls, then a 260px panel for mod assets, layers (base/paint/AI candidate), and history, leading into a canvas stage with checkerboard transparency, pixel grid, zoom, and a coordinate readout above a palette strip.

For the right side, I'm settling on a 340px panel with a compact Preview always visible at top, and tabs below for Cyrus/Checks/History, matching the real inspector style. Below everything, I'm adding a bottom prompt dock styled like the real Cyrus prompt-shell with a conic border, letting users ask Cyrus to edit the texture and generate a new candidate.

For the Cyrus candidate card, I'm sketching a before/after diff view with onion/split/side toggles, a changes list, quality delta, and Accept/Apply-part/Reject actions, plus a canvas overlay preview on hover. I want to keep the asset examples coherent around one mod rather than mixing Frost Blade assets into a Banshee Hunt scenario.

For the actual candidate story, I'm thinking the glock_9mm asset is a good target: its palette size (49) exceeds the 32-color limit, so Cyrus proposes reducing grip noise to shrink the palette and pass the check. The "partly apply" flow would let the user pick which op-level changes from the candidate to accept, starting with removing the grip noise op.

Now I'm designing the pixel canvas editor: layered RGBA compositing with tools like pencil, eraser, flood fill, color picker, line, rectangle, and a rectangular marquee selection to constrain edits, plus undo/redo, zoom range, grid toggle, and mirror mode. I'm also planning how the palette gets organized into shaded ramps (metal, etc.) derived via HSL shifts for a lit top-left look.

I'm sketching out a Style DNA strip summarizing the mod's consistent rules—outline color, light direction, ramp depth, noise off, max palette count—shown as chips with real thresholds, plus a preview panel with tiled texture view, generic hotbar/inventory slots (avoiding Mojang assets), and a simple 2D "in-hand" representation since 3D is out of scope.

For the in-hand sprite, I'm weighing a flat rotated view versus faking Minecraft's extruded-item look using stacked CSS layers with depth offsets to simulate thickness cheaply, though that risks conflicting with the earlier decision to skip 3D previews.

I'll keep the quality checks panel running real texture analysis on every edit, listing check names like transparency, palette size, contrast, noise, outline, and vanilla lookalike with actual computed values and limits rather than invented numbers, alongside an asset history showing real revisions with thumbnails and restore buttons. For the Sound Studio, I'm laying out a left panel listing the "banshee" sound set's event slots like ambient and hurt.

For the center panel, I'm building out the detailed event editor: a namespaced header with role, category, and required subtitle field, variant tabs with weights, a waveform canvas with time ruler, trim handles, fade curves, gain envelope, zoom, transport controls, and a layered lane stack showing mini-waveforms positioned by offset.

On the right, I'm laying out tabs for Library, Synth, Checks, and History — Library handles search and tagging with an audition/add-as-layer flow, Synth gives preset cards with real parameter sliders, and Checks surfaces actual measured audio stats (true peak, loudness, silence ratio, DC offset) alongside LUFS and true peak meters. I'm thinking a compact always-visible "Meters" strip under the waveform would make the Checks data persistently useful rather than tab-hidden.

For audio playback, synth layers render real WebAudio output while library layers use a shaped-noise proxy matching the manifest duration with lowpass filtering and an envelope — and I want the layer row to honestly label this as a preview proxy since real library audio stays on the render host.

Now sketching the Mod assets inspector page: a header with mod name, Minecraft version/loader, and a texture section with cards for individual assets, weighing whether to include mob skin reuse notes consistent with the master plan.

Since the texture DSL only covers item textures, I'll skip editable mob skins but add an honest "not yet editable" row for entity skins to avoid implying functionality that doesn't exist. Then I'm laying out sound event rows for each mob/weapon action with variant counts, subtitles, and play/edit buttons, plus a pack status card using clearly placeholder mock data for things like file size.

I want to avoid fabricated usage stats, but keep realistic pack status details: whether the resource pack is required or optional, how it behaves for players who decline, and that Bedrock players via Geyser see vanilla looks since this is a Java resource pack. I'll add a segmented control to demo different pack states — hosted, not hosted yet, delivery off — plus a server-side pack loader status indicator.

For the locked states page, I'm designing a plan switcher (Free, Katara, Saka, All models) that shows the studio dock with locked cards like "Texture Studio — needs All models plan" and "Sound Studio — needs Saka plan or higher," while making clear existing assets can always be kept, installed, and exported regardless of plan — only creating or editing new content is gated. I'm also including a downgrade example showing a sound falling back to vanilla, plus an upgrade CTA.

I'm also thinking through a "plan unknown" state with a retry option, and considering whether to add a floating, visually distinct "mockup controls" panel (theme, plan, viewport) across all four mockup files so the asset view can respect plan state too, while keeping the real topbar theme toggle consistent with how Cyrus follows the portal's actual theme.

I'll place the theme toggle in the topbar for realism, use a dashed-border "Mockup" pill in the bottom-left for plan switching, and support URL params for screenshots. I also need to design a narrow mobile layout with read-only preview-and-approve flows for both texture and sound views, built with media queries and separate markup sections — a sizable build, so I'll start by carefully writing the shared CSS and reuse the handoff UI icons.

Checking which icons exist already versus which I need to draw myself in the same 24-grid, 1.7-stroke style with rounded caps and light fill accents...

content.thinking:
Happy with the hooded banshee head and cyan eyes design, I'm moving on to writing common.css, setting up the design tokens and the overall shell structure with a collapsed portal rail and a studio area with a subtle gradient background.

For the component styles, I'm deciding to keep to a single accent color as the brief requires — using a solid violet primary button with an inset highlight, saving the brand gradient for logo marks only. I'm also planning panel headers with small uppercase mono eyebrows and inspector-style tabs with icons, labels, and count badges.

Now I'm sketching the actual layout dimensions: a 1440x900 desktop grid with a 56px rail, 248px left panel, flexible center, and 352px right panel, plus a 60px topbar. For the texture studio center column, I'm budgeting vertical space across a 44px toolbar, ~480px canvas, ~120px palette panel, and a ~96px prompt dock, with a floating tool rail inside the canvas area and a right-side preview card with tabs for Tile/Slot/Hand views.

On the left panel I'm planning a mod assets list, a layers panel with eye/lock/opacity toggles, and a history panel distinguishing session undo steps from saved asset revisions. For the JS state model, I'm defining layers as objects with id, name, kind, visibility, lock, opacity, and pixel data, where a generated base layer renders from spec and a paint layer sits non-destructively on top with alpha-based erasing.

To let erasing punch through the generated base without destroying it, I'm adding a cut mask alongside the paint pixels — compositing checks cut first (transparent), then paint alpha, then falls back to the base. For candidate layers shown during preview, accepting replaces the base spec with a new revision, partial accept applies only selected sub-changes via checkboxes, and reject just dismisses the candidate.

For rendering, I'm drawing the canvas with smoothing disabled, faint per-pixel grid lines with heavier lines every 4-8 pixels, a checkerboard backdrop, and a hover highlight with coordinate/color readout. I also want quality checks to rerun automatically on each composite change, plus preview modes (tiled, hotbar slot, held-in-hand) with a light/dark backdrop toggle, and a palette view that groups the spec's color keys into hand-defined ramps.

Now I'm planning ramp generation: a button to auto-create a 4-5 shade ramp from a chosen swatch using an HSL-based lightness/hue shift (cooler shadows, warmer highlights) following good pixel-art conventions. I also want a "style DNA" strip showing rule chips (outline color, light direction, ramp depth, no noise/gradients, palette cap, transparent background) with a consistency indicator across the mod's textures, plus an "Apply DNA to all textures" action that generates candidate fixes.

For the prompt dock, I'm unsure whether to show a specific token cost estimate since the real spec calls for "cost estimates per asset op" but doesn't define the number — I'll settle for a model chip (Yakko) and a note that cost is shown before running, flagging this as an open question for the project owner.

For Sound Studio, I'm thinking through rendering banshee and glock variant data from SoundSpec, using a layered renderer with a loader proxy for shared library layers, and drawing a waveform on canvas with min/max sampling per pixel column and an accent-colored gradient fill, along with region markers.

I'm also working out trim regions (shaded outside bounds), triangular fade-curve handles, and a cyan playhead, with interactions for dragging trim/fade handles, zooming via buttons or wheel, clicking to set the playhead, and playback through WebAudio by converting PCM data to a Float32 AudioBuffer — gain sliders per layer trigger re-render and live measurement updates. For the layer stack, each lane shows a source chip and a mini-waveform positioned by start offset, with gain, pitch, and offset controls plus mute/solo, and options to add layers from Library, Synth, or Silence. I'm also adding validation so an empty subtitle field triggers required-field error styling and a red dot on the event slot, since checkSoundSpec should reject missing subtitles — displaying the relevant language key for players with subtitles enabled.

For the subtitle, I realize the compiler actually generates the key from the subtitle text, so I need a text input with a mono key preview instead. The Library panel needs a search input, group chips from SOUND_GROUPS, a category selector with real counts, and list rows showing play button, filename, category, duration, and LUFS with an "Add" button, plus a header showing total sound count and licence status — though I'm unsure how much to surface the unverified/no-redistribution licence question in the UI. Since there's no real bundled audio, I'll have the audition button just animate progress with an explanatory caption, while the Synth tab gets preset cards with real waveform thumbnails and parameter sliders, and the Checks tab needs real validation logic.

Now I'm thinking through the Checks tab showing soundQuality results and meters per variant, plus aggregated slot status per event, and a History tab with waveform diff overlays comparing before/after revisions. I also want to add a lightweight AI touch — a "Cyrus suggests" candidate variant with A/B audition and accept/reject controls, shown as a dashed-border candidate card on the hurt event to demonstrate the pattern without overbuilding it. For narrow layouts under 760px, I'm planning a collapsed view showing header, asset preview, checks summary, candidate approval card, and history list instead of the full editor.

For the mod assets page, I'm designing it with a Cyrus topbar and a mod header card showing icon, name, category, and version, followed by pack status, textures grid, and a sound events table grouped by set with edit links into the texture/sound studios. I'm leaning toward styling it like a real inspector panel with tabs, placed over a simplified static network map (core orb, Minecraft node, Creatures, mod pill) to visually tie it back to the main product.

For the locked states case, I'm reusing the same inspector Assets tab layout but adding a plan switcher so it can show Free/Katara/Saka/All-models locked variations, keeping the inspector width around 540px for this tab.

Rather than faking a broken editor, I'll show a clean read-only viewer of the texture so viewing and exporting still work, with a lock bar explaining that editing needs the All models plan — keeping the restriction honest rather than feeling broken.

Since the plan state is unknown, I'll keep upgrade copy generic: "Texture Studio is part of the All models plan," with an "Upgrade to All models" button leading to "See Cyrus plans," avoiding any pricing. I'll use the plan labels Free, Katara, Saka, and All models, treating "top plan" as All models. Time to start writing, beginning with common.css.

content.thinking:
The rail icon can stay white-on-dark since it sits on a dark island. Now I'm setting up the Texture Studio's main grid layout, with a three-column structure for the workspace and a left panel for mod text.

I'm planning the center column with a toolbar, canvas stage with floating zoom controls, and dock, plus a right side with preview and tabbed panels. I'm also working out canvas sizing and zoom defaults for different grid sizes, and designing how the compare modes (current/candidate/split/onion) would render over the stage with a draggable divider.

For diff mode I want changed pixels outlined in cyan against a dimmed base. I'm also designing partial-apply checkboxes so users can select individual changes before accepting a candidate, with the button label reflecting how many of the total changes are selected, while keeping paint layers intact above the base spec. For undo/history, I'm storing full state snapshots (paint, cut, spec) per step so clicking a history entry can jump back, and sketching how asset revision history would list entries with labels.

I'm also thinking through what happens when a studio edit is saved: it should create a new revision, which then needs the pack to be rebuilt and re-hosted before the change takes effect in the next mod build.

For the preview panel, I'm sketching tabs for Tile, Hotbar, and In-hand views, plus a light/dark background toggle to check readability. I'll mock up a generic 9-slot hotbar with bevel-edged squares (avoiding Mojang art) showing the glock and veil items in the first couple slots.

The Checks tab shows a verdict and issue list, maybe with a mod-wide summary count. The Cyrus tab shows a candidate suggestion card, so I'm linking the quality warning (49-colour palette) to a "Fix with Cyrus" button that auto-generates a fix candidate for the user to review.

I'm also sketching the reference-image-to-spec feature mentioned in the master plan but deciding to skip it as a later open question. For the prompt dock, I'm designing a chip showing the active edit target, an input hint clarifying that prompts create candidates rather than overwrite anything, a model selector, and a send action that produces a busy state before returning a new candidate card. The palette panel will list each colour ramp for the texture under a labeled header.

I'm detailing palette panel contents: each ramp has swatches with a selection ring, a counter against the DSL colour limit, and a "Generate ramp" feature producing shades to add. Below that sits a Style DNA strip showing style chips, texture-following status, and an "Apply to all textures" action, plus a vertical glass tool rail with pencil, eraser, fill, picker, select, line, and rectangle tools each bound to keyboard shortcuts.

Now I'm working out the top toolbar: a thumbnail and label for the current asset, then a size control. Since assets differ in native size (veil at 16px, glock at 32px), I'm deciding to show the canvas size readonly but allow a toggle between 16/32/64, where resizing triggers a candidate redraw at the new spec size.

Beyond that, I need undo/redo, zoom controls, and a primary "Save revision" button, plus a coordinates readout at the bottom-left (pixel position, color, selection) and a zoom readout at bottom-right. For narrow screens I'm planning a simplified header with a large checkered preview, name, verdict badge, a compact before/after candidate card with Accept/Reject, a condensed checks summary, history, and a note explaining that detailed editing needs a larger screen. Now I'll start writing texture.html with inline styles.

This foundation looks promising but has a few issues: the body text shouldn't be monospace, row buttons need left-aligned text instead of centered, and links should lose their underline and inherit the surrounding text color. The wordmark itself renders fine since it's using the actual stylized dark asset.

Other fixes needed: the dark palette swatches need a subtle ring to stand out against the background, and the Style DNA chips are wrapping awkwardly — I should set them to nowrap with shorter labels like "Outline #101113", "Top-left light", "3–5 shade ramps", "No noise", and "Clear background" instead of the current cramped text. The compare bar text also needs nowrap so it doesn't break mid-sentence, and the right panel's candidate card needs a shorter preview stage height with the cluttered qdelta tags removed or simplified so the accept buttons aren't cut off at the bottom.

The hotbar is overflowing its container (9 slots at 36px exceeds the 316px width), so I should shrink slots to 30px. The left column's empty-feeling Edit steps panel could use a hint like "Every stroke is one step. Click a step to go back to it." to fill the space meaningfully, and I'm now checking why the Current/Candidate splitter labels aren't rendering — looks like a positioning issue where the span is tied to a zero-width splitter element.

I'll just move those labels to the bottom of the canvas instead of debugging the overflow further. The "Candidate · not applied" text and warn tag styling both look right, and the eyebrow typography matches the hierarchy style fine. Now I want to check the light theme and a narrower viewport.

Light mode checks out, and the Glock renders well against the dark preview backdrop and narrow layouts. I'm noting a few CSS fixes to make: links inheriting color without underlines, left-aligning row text, and adjusting the DNA chip styling.

More fixes: shortening labels to prevent wrapping in cmpbar, setting hotbar slot size to 30, replacing qdelta with a single-line summary on candidate cards, making the tabpane flex and scrollable, and adjusting prev stage height. I also need to figure out why the splitter labels are invisible — tracing through the positioning logic, I realize the cmpbar's z-index is higher than the splitter's, so it's likely just covering the labels rather than them being missing entirely.

I'll move the splitter labels to the bottom of the canvas to avoid the cmpbar overlap, add a hint for the empty edit steps section, shorten the dock placeholder text, simplify the cost estimate display, truncate the asset list kind label to "drop item," and consider offering a background toggle for the checkerboard pattern competing with dark-colored items in dark mode.

I'll add a small backdrop mode segment (checker/dark/light) to the HUD, cheap but useful since other pixel editors offer this. Comparing against the real reference design, my topbar crumbs and panels look close enough, and the palette swatches are fine as-is for this item. Time to apply all these fixes.

content.thinking:
I'm thinking through how a library proxy loader could synthesize placeholder audio by group type—using sharp noise envelopes for impacts/gunshots, formant-modulated noise for voice/screams, and swelling bandpass noise for whooshes—mapping each category to corresponding synth presets as stand-ins.

Now I'm drafting the actual Banshee SoundSpec with its hostile category and event variants: ambient moans blending a wail synth with wind library audio, hurt shrieks mixing synth and sampled screams with weighted variants, a death event that's currently missing its required subtitle, an attack combining a swoosh sample with a growl synth, and a step event where Banshee's floating movement suggests using silence instead of a footstep sound.

But I'm reconsidering that silence approach for the step slot since a fully silent clip would fail the audible quality check requiring some peak level — instead I should either leave the step event out and mark the base mob silent, or use a very quiet whoosh sample at low gain. I'm also thinking I could use the silence primitive constructively as a spacer between two wail bursts in the "Wail of the Banshee" ability sequence.

I'm filling out the rest of the mob/item sets: the ability slot gets a simple subtitle, spawn stays empty for the user to add, and the glock set covers fire (with layered gunshot sample plus synth crack) and reload (sample plus a delayed click), with no ambient needed. That matches the full requested role list across mob and item categories, and I'm assigning the namespace key nx_7k2qf9.

For the waveform editor itself, I'm working out that the main display should show the normalized post-processed mix the player actually hears, since renderVariant applies loudness targets and limiting at that stage. But trim, fade, and gain controls live per-layer in the spec, so selecting a layer in the stack should overlay that layer's own region on top of the mix timeline rather than replacing the view entirely.

Dragging a layer's start offset, trim window, fade handles, or gain line directly edits that layer's fields in the spec, and "regions" just refers to these per-layer overlays on the timeline. For gain, I want a dB slider plus a draggable gain line, while the overall variant's auto-normalization gets surfaced truthfully in the meters as something like "auto gain +3.2 dB to reach −14 LUFS," pulled straight from renderVariant's output.

For the per-lane mini-waveforms, I'm weighing whether to render each layer individually with renderVariant (which normalizes) and then rescale by its gain, or render directly from the raw synth output so the shape reflects true amplitude — leaning toward a single-layer normalized render scaled by relative gain for simplicity.

I still need to figure out the timeline display with zoom/scroll, playback via AudioContext with a playhead and loop toggle, and the metering panel showing LUFS, true peak, silence ratio, and duration checks against role targets using CY.measure and CY.soundQuality.

Now I'm sketching the 1440x900 layout: a left sidebar with sound event slots grouped by mob/item, and a center panel with an event header showing the key, role, category, and subtitle field, plus variant tabs for each weighted variant.

I'm fleshing out the waveform editor toolbar, layer stack with gain/pitch/fade controls per lane, and processing options like lowpass/reverb/echo, then the right column's quality meters and Library/Synth/Checks/History tabs, plus a dock below.

I'm deciding the prompt dock sits at the bottom of the center column, and checking the height budget fits within 840px with room to spare. Now I'm starting to write sound.html, mindful that reverb rendering may be heavier than the earlier synth's 13ms and should debounce re-renders on slider changes via rAF.

content.thinking: Checking that the global LIB constant doesn't collide with the placeholder syntax—it shouldn't since those are just string templates. I also confirm the library-subset categories list covers the full 163 categories as expected.

This is looking solid and polished overall. The selected layer index at the start seems fine, and the waveform region ending before the reverb tail continues makes sense. The violet saturation is quite bright and could feel a bit heavy, though that fits the neon aesthetic being referenced.

More importantly, I need to look at why reload shows a failing red dot while fire only warns — it's likely a proxy artifact where the 'click' synth used for gun loading produces a short burst then silence, tripping a silence-ratio check. Since the proxies distort what's actually realistic, I should tune them so most events pass, one shows a warn (fire is a good candidate to demonstrate that state), and keep death red intentionally since its subtitle is missing. The "HURT" tag next to banshee.hurt also feels slightly redundant and worth reconsidering.

Looking at smaller UI details now: the variants row and hint text wrapping are fine, meters look correctly placed, but file names like "Hit - Fade Out.MP3" need extension-stripping logic that's case-insensitive and trims extra whitespace. The tabs row is also cramped at narrow widths — History gets cut off because four tabs with counts don't fit, so I should shorten labels, drop the Synth count, and tighten spacing. Lastly, I'm second-guessing using cyan for synth-layer waveforms since cyan is supposed to be reserved for "live" selection states only, so I may need to shift layer-kind colors to keep that rule consistent.

I'm deciding that layer kinds should be distinguished by icon and label rather than color, with all lanes using the accent color at varying opacity and full opacity for the selected lane; since the selected waveform region already uses cyan, I'll keep the selected mini-lane cyan too for visual linking, while kind chips stay neutral. I also want to verify the verdict logic against the actual code, so I'm planning to write a quick node script that extracts and evaluates the SETS block from the engine and library files directly rather than running it through a browser.

Now I'm moving on to designing mod-assets.html: a dimmed network background on the left with an inspector panel on the right, tabs for Code, Explain, Versions, Files, Notes, and the active Assets tab, plus a header with icon tile, breadcrumb, title "Banshee Hunt," subtitle, status pill, and close button.

For the Assets tab I'm laying out a resource pack status card showing hosted state, sha1 hash, delivery behavior, and mock server install info, along with a control to toggle between pack states like Hosted, Not hosted, Delivery off, or version-gated. Below that I'm starting a textures section with a grid of thumbnail cards.

I'm sketching the texture cards (checkered thumbnail, name, size, quality tag, edit link to texture.html) plus a non-editable mob skin row, then a sounds section with per-event table rows linking to sound.html, and footer buttons for opening the Texture Studio and Sound Studio.

input.content:
# Cyrus Texture and Sound Studios: design notes (mockups, 2026-10-10)

Files: `texture-studio.html`, `sound-studio.html`, `mod-assets.html`, `locked-states.html` (self-contained; editable sources in `src/`, rebuilt by `tools/build.py`), screenshots in `shots/`.

## Principles
- **Polish in place, no new look.** Tokens, type and chrome are copied from the v5 handoff (`app/dashboard/cyrus/studio.css`): deep space `#05030b`, glass panels, Inter + Space Grotesk + JetBrains Mono, the TopBar crumbs, the conic-rim prompt dock, the inspector tab anatomy, the handoff's 1.7-stroke icon set. The asset entry is a new **Assets** tab in the existing inspector, over the network map.
- **One accent.** Violet is the only accent. Cyan only means "live": the playhead, the selected layer, the compare splitter. Green, amber and red only mean pass, warn and fail.
- **Truth first.** The mockups run the repo's real code (bundled from `lib/cyrus/textures` and `lib/cyrus/sound`). Quality panels show real `tq-1`/`sq-1` results, so the Glock really warns on `palette_size` (49) and the gunshots really warn on loudness after peak limiting. Library rows are real manifest metadata. The only stand-in is library *audio* (it stays on the render host), and the page says so.
- **AI never overwrites.** Every Cyrus edit arrives as a candidate. You can compare it, apply part of it, or reject it.
- **Light mode is designed**, not inverted: white glass, inked colours, light checkerboard. The portal rail stays a dark island in both themes, as it does in the portal.

## Mapping to backend data
| Screen | Data |
|---|---|
| Texture canvas, layers | `TextureSpec` (generated base, locked) + a raster Paint layer on top. Accepting a candidate swaps the spec. The PNG is a build artifact. |
| Palette, ramps | `spec.palette` (max 24, `MAX_PALETTE`). Ramps are UI groupings; "New ramp" generates 5 hue-shifted shades. |
| Style DNA | The prompt's CUSTOM TEXTURES rules (one outline colour, top-left light, 3-5 shade ramps, no noise or gradients, clear background); compliance is measured with the `noise` and `outline` checks. |
| Checks | `textureQuality()`: `transparency`, `palette_size`, `contrast`, `noise`, `outline`, `vanilla_lookalike` (`not_run`). `soundQuality()`: `format`, `true_peak`, `loudness`, `audible`, `silence_ratio`, `dc_offset`, `duration`, plus a subtitle row. |
| Sound events | `SoundSpec`: sets → events (`role`, `category`, required `subtitle`) → 1-4 weighted variants → up to 4 layers (`lib:` / `synth:` / `silence`, with gain, pitch, start, trim, fades) + processing. The key is `nx_<8>:<set>.<event>`. |
| Meters | `measure()` + `ROLE_PROFILE` bands; auto gain and peak limiting come from `renderVariant()`. |
| Pack status | R0/R1 sync states: hosted, delivery off (`CYRUS_MANAGED_PLUGINS_REAL` off), unhosted; `required: false`; the Bedrock line from `assetLines`. |
| Locks | `canAsset(plan, kind, op)`, ported 1:1. Only create/edit is gated. The copy is the gate's own `reason` strings and the `downgradeSpecAssets` notice. |
| History | Asset revisions (spec + render + quality per revision). Restoring makes a new revision. |

## Component inventory (React)
- `StudioShell({studio, mod, plan})`: TopBar crumbs, Texture/Sound switch, token chip.
- `PixelCanvas({raster, zoom, grid, mirror, backdrop, tool, selection, compare})`, `ToolRail({tool, mirror, grid, color})`, `CompareBar({mode: split|onion|diff|after})`.
- `LayerList({layers, active, onToggle})`, `EditSteps({steps, at, onJump})`.
- `PaletteStrip({palette, ramps, color, usedCount})`, `RampGenerator({from})`, `StyleDnaStrip({rules, follows})`.
- `LivePreview({raster, mode: hotbar|hand|tile, bg})`.
- `CandidateCard({before, after, changes[], picks, qualityDelta, onAccept, onApplyPart, onApplyInSelection, onReject})`, shared by both studios.
- `QualityPanel({report})`, `CheckRow({id, status, value, limit, message})`.
- `EventList({sets, selected})`, `EventHeader({key, role, category, subtitle, onSubtitle})` (states: valid, missing).
- `VariantTabs({variants, candidate, weights})`, `WaveformEditor({pcm, layer, zoom, playhead, onTrim, onFade, onMove})`, `LayerLane({layer, solo, selected})`, `FxRow({processing})`.
- `LoudnessMeters({measure, role, gainDb, peakLimited})`, `LibraryBrowser({query, group, category, items})`, `SynthPicker({preset, params})`.
- `AssetsTab({mod, pack, textures, soundSets, plan})`, `PackStatusCard({state})`.
- `StudioLock({kind, decision})` (states: locked, plan_unknown, included), `PlanMatrix({plan})`, `DowngradeNotice({denials})`.

## Interaction details
- Texture tools: B, E, G, I, M, L, U; X = mirror, # = grid, +/- = zoom, Ctrl+wheel zooms, Esc clears the selection, Ctrl Z / Ctrl Shift Z undo and redo. Every stroke is one step. Partial apply works per change (checkboxes) or inside the selection.
- Sound: Space plays, L loops. Drag a layer's edges to trim, its top corners to fade, its body to move it. Sliders re-render live. A/B plays V1, then the candidate.
- Quality checks re-run on every edit.
- On a narrow screen the page is read-only: preview, checks, play, approve or reject. Approving saves a revision.

## Accessibility
Focus rings on every control; tools carry `aria-pressed` and shortcut hints; the subtitle field is `aria-required`, with an inline error; status is never colour alone (icon + word + value); text contrast uses the AA-tuned v5 inks; reduced motion stops the rim and spin animations. Open: the canvas and the waveform need keyboard pixel and handle movement (arrow keys + Enter) and screen-reader summaries.

## Deliberately not included
3D model or block preview (the "In hand" view is a flat extrusion), mob-skin UV editing (shown as "later"), animation and `.mcmeta`, reference-image-to-spec, image-model or AI-audio providers, spectrum view and pitch-preserving stretch, Texture Library contents (no source exists yet), prices.

## Open questions for the owner
1. Plan naming: the gate says Free / Katara / Saka / **All models** (Yakko); the handoff says Sokka/Yako. Which spelling is final?
2. Token cost per asset edit: the dock shows no estimate because there is no measured price yet. Should it show one, and when?
3. Should packs be optional on join (current default) or required?
4. Library licence: the bundle licence forbids redistributing the files. Do processed sounds inside customers' packs comply (legal check)?
5. Should the mob-skin row stay visible as "later", or be hidden until it's built?
6. Should mobile approvals be allowed, or should mobile be view-only?
7. Inspector width: Assets needs about 560px versus 480 today. Widen just this tab, or open the studios full-page?

input.message:
All four mockups are built in the real v5 Cyrus look and rendered through Playwright on node-2, in the capped agents slice. The node-2 copy is deleted afterwards.

**Files** (each mockup is one self-contained HTML file):
- `/root/agent-notes/cyrus-designs/texture-studio.html`: a working pixel editor. 32×32 Glock and 16×16 banshee veil, tool rail with shortcuts, zoom, grid, mirror, undo steps and layers (locked generated base plus a paint layer). Palette with ramps you can generate, a mod-wide Style DNA strip, and a live hotbar / in-hand / tile preview on dark or light. A Cyrus candidate can be compared split, onion or changed-pixels, applied in part, or rejected. The checks are live, and asset history is included.
- `/root/agent-notes/cyrus-designs/sound-studio.html`: banshee and handgun event slots, weighted variants, and a required subtitle field. Waveform with drag trim, fade and move, layer lanes, effects, loudness and true-peak meters, the library browser, the synth presets with their real parameters, and an A/B candidate.
- `/root/agent-notes/cyrus-designs/mod-assets.html`: a new Assets tab in the inspector, over the network map. Shows pack status (hosted / delivery off / unhosted), the Bedrock note, and Edit buttons.
- `/root/agent-notes/cyrus-designs/locked-states.html`: Free, Katara, Saka, All models and "plan unknown". Locked studios stay view-only or listen-only, with the gate's own copy and downgrade notices.
- `DESIGN-NOTES.md` (886 words), 17 PNGs in `shots/`, sources in `src/`.

All four have dark and light themes and a narrow review-and-approve view. They run the repo's real code: the checks show real results, so the Glock genuinely warns on palette size (49 colours). Library audio stays on the render host, so audition plays a labelled stand-in.

**Fixed after reviewing the screenshots:** canvas checkerboard too dark, cramped Style DNA strip, colours beyond the one accent, network nodes hidden behind the inspector, a flat core redrawn as the particle nebula, a clipped tab, and a fake "reload fails" caused by the stand-in audio.

**Owner decisions:**
1. Final plan and model spelling: the gate says Saka / All models (Yakko), the handoff says Sokka / Yako.
2. Should the prompt dock show a token cost per asset edit?
3. Packs optional or required on join?
4. Library licence for processed sounds in customer packs.
5. Show "mob skin: later" or hide it?
6. Approvals on mobile?
7. Widen the inspector to about 560px, or open the studios full-page?
